title: Two-Phase Holographic Cosmology from a Gravitational O(4) Wall: Conditional Reconstruction of the Late Dark-Energy Scale
description: A frozen conditional SFV/dSB two-phase cosmology built on the published gravitational O(4)/Coleman-De Luccia wall. The Lorentzian thick wall supplies an early dS3 accelerated phase. At the single phenomenological history datum N_star=57.8401844744, a delocalizing non-destructive 2+1 to 3+1 holographic handoff fixes a global screen radius R_star=85.993 micrometers and resolution R_star^-1=2.294686 meV. After separating local microscopic response from the nonlocal finite-screen sector, a discrete maximal-depth CKN-shaped reconstruction rule L_IR=sqrt(3) Mbar_4 R_star^2 yields L_IR=1.580518e26 m, H_late=1.248496e-42 GeV, and rho_DE=2.772638e-47 GeV^4. Within this convention rho_DE=R_star^-4 exactly and the late global/extrinsic dS4 geometry gives w=-1 without a dark-energy scalar. The absolute late normalization is explicitly conditional because N_star is not yet action-derived and the maximal-depth normalization remains a discrete holographic postulate. Primordial A_s and n_s are also retained phenomenologically after explicit current-action no-go tests. DOI: 10.5281/zenodo.22071079.
